plan.title: [framework-gap] Initial installation commit blocked by prospective scope-cover despite documented pre-activation bootstrap

narratives.Description: After directive init, the git commit hook refuses the commit of Directive's installed files when no scope is running, although the getting-started docs commit them before the first scope, and activating a scope does not help because the gate reads file_scope from the merge base. The same refusal hits current-layout upgrade and repair commits, including the pin bump in package.json and the lockfile, and it points people at writing a chore brief. The fix drops each staged entry whose raw path is canonical, whose modes are plain files, whose blobs read cleanly, and whose change classifyDirectiveOwnedChange calls directive-only; a commit of only such entries needs no scope, and everything else still needs cover.
narratives.Overview:
1. Directive-only drop (P1, P2, P3). In `evaluateProspectiveScopeCover` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`), after the lifecycle filter, drop from the product set each staged entry that passes items 2 and 3 and whose change `classifyDirectiveOwnedChange(rel, headText, stagedText)` returns `directive-only`. Dropping is by raw staged entry, before path normalization, so a distinct raw path that normalizes to the same string is never dropped with it. When the product set is then empty, return ok before the story binding and the ready-scope check, with a message that names the dropped paths.
2. Eligibility (P4). An entry is a candidate only when its raw git path equals its canonical form (no backslash, no leading or trailing whitespace, no leading `./`), its staged mode is `100644` or `100755` (or the entry is a deletion), and its HEAD mode, when present, is `100644` or `100755`. Symlinks (`120000`), gitlinks (`160000`) and any other mode stay product.
3. Blob reads (P4). Resolve HEAD once. HEAD is unborn only when `HEAD` is a symbolic ref to a branch that does not exist; any other resolution failure is an error. For a resolved commit, look up the exact path in its tree; a successful lookup with no entry is absent; an entry is read by its object id. Absent or unborn gives `null`. Any resolution, lookup or blob-read error keeps the path product. A staged blob that cannot be read on a non-deletion keeps the path product; an empty blob is content, not a failure. Readers are optional seams for tests.
4. Unchanged rails (P4). With no raw staged entries (the `listStagedRelPaths` seam), nothing is dropped. `mixed` and `not-owned` stay product. In a commit that also holds other paths, only the dropped entries leave the set; the rest still need cover. `MANAGED_HOOK_DEPOSIT_REL_PATHS`, the `xbrief/` and `vbrief/` prefixes, planning publication (#5839), the merge-gate warn sites (#6535), `classifyDirectiveOwnedChange` and `installerManagedMatchers()` are unchanged.
5. Refusal reasons (#5949). The gate records one exact reason for each staged path it keeps: `unreadable-head`, `unreadable-staged`, `unsupported-mode`, `non-canonical-path`, `mixed` or `not-owned`. The existing scope and fence causes (no ready running scope, unreadable fence, no positive governing allow, outside `file_scope`) keep their current wording. When the staged set holds Directive paths, the refusal names each kept path with its reason and names the dropped paths. Only when at least one path was dropped does it add the recovery: commit the dropped Directive-only paths on their own and cover the rest with the story's scope. It does not suggest writing, promoting or activating a new brief for Directive paths. A refusal with no Directive paths staged keeps today's text.
6. Unit tests (P1-P4). In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.test.ts`: an install set (new `AGENTS.md` scaffold with the managed section, `package.json` scaffold with the Directive dependency, lockfile, `MINIMAL_TASKFILE`, managed `.gitignore` lines, a skill pointer, a hook outer, a host hook config, `.githooks/pre-commit`, `.deft/GENERATION.json`) passes with no ready scope; a current-layout upgrade set (new hook outer, deleted old hook outer, pin bump in `package.json` and the lockfile, managed-section change) passes; `package.json` with an added app dependency and `AGENTS.md` with a new user paragraph outside the managed section stay uncovered; the no-entries `package.json` case at 3821-3829 is unchanged; a HEAD read error, a staged read failure, a symlink, a gitlink, a backslash path, a whitespace-padded path, and a backslash path staged beside its canonical twin stay product; an empty staged blob is classified, not refused; a mixed commit leaves only the non-Directive path uncovered; the refusal text names the dropped paths and each kept path with its reason, does not mention `scope:promote` or `scope:activate`, and gives no commit-the-Directive-part recovery when nothing was dropped.
7. Setup test (P1, P3). In `packages/runtime/src/`, one test runs real setup into a temporary git repository, stages the whole deposit, and shows `evaluateProspectiveScopeCover` with the real git readers and no scope admits it; then a second setup run that rewrites managed files (repair after the `AGENTS.md` managed section is edited) is staged and admitted the same way. The test is named as gate-admission proof, not local commit success.
8. CI regression (#5949). A test builds a valid fixture repository whose unrelated `check:merge` prerequisites are met, commits a base, then commits a head that adds or changes only Directive deposit paths (no brief, no running scope), and runs the actual `check:merge` gate composition on that real base-to-head diff, including `verify:scope-provenance`; it passes. The base is resolvable as the merge base the gate reads, and the test asserts that `verify:scope-provenance` evaluated the diff rather than reporting the no-merge-base skip (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` 858-870). If a check refuses because of the deposit itself, the fix narrows only that scope refusal for Directive-only paths, through the same rules as items 1-3; unrelated failures are not changed.

- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, `not-owned` and `mixed` paths, and a commit with no raw staged entries, keep today's scope-cover result, and the existing hook-deposit and lifecycle admissions are unchanged.
- In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, a scope-cover refusal for a set that holds Directive paths names the dropped paths and each kept path with one exact reason, keeps the existing scope and fence causes, gives the commit-the-Directive-part recovery only when a path was dropped, and does not suggest writing, promoting or activating a brief.

narratives.Constraint:

- Gate-side exact-output or block rules for shared files in this unit; their precision belongs to the ownership API (operator restatement in Stop 1 7020826034; #6790).

The agent's `git commit` hook refuses that commit: prospective scope-cover treats `AGENTS.md`, `Taskfile.yml`, `package.json`, the lockfile and the installed skill pointers as product files, and product files need a running scope whose `file_scope` is on the merge base. The report is from 0.126.1. From 0.130 setup also replaces Directive's git hooks on upgrade (#6716), so installs and upgrades will produce these commits more often.

The recommended fix lets the commit gate drop each staged path whose change that API calls Directive-only, using the HEAD and staged contents. A commit made only of such paths needs no scope. Answers: **1.** Keep the six existing exemptions in this unit, as R4 requires; acknowledge that mixed host-config changes already bypass coverage. **2.** Path-only ownership is acceptable only as an explicit reservation of those filenames, not proof that their contents came from Directive. **3.** Keep the real-setup test and add an upgrade case; the pending upgrade fixture complements rather than replaces first-install coverage.

**4.** Other local checks remain: notably `verify:branch` can refuse a default-branch commit. I found no basis for claiming every clean feature-branch deposit necessarily fails forward coverage: its source extensions exclude `.mjs`. **5.** Read HEAD through a result distinguishing present, absent, and error; only proven absence becomes `null`.

**Failure mode:** Clean installer changes to `greptile.json`, `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml`, and deletion of `.github/workflows/deft-core-guard.yml` remain `not-owned` and require scope. The first two can occur during install or repair too. Lifecycle seeds are also not API-owned, but correctly retain their existing exemption.

**Disposition:** Make these API gaps explicit dependencies or narrow the claimed acceptance boundary. Prefer upstream content-aware ownership fixes over requiring another operator commit or brief. R5 must cover actual setup modifications and removals, not only its fresh-file list.

When the product set is then empty, return ok before the story binding and the ready-scope check, with a message that names the dropped paths.
2. Eligibility (P4). An entry is a candidate only when its raw git path equals its canonical form (no backslash, no leading or trailing whitespace, no leading `./`), its staged mode is `100644` or `100755` (or the entry is a deletion), and its HEAD mode, when present, is `100644` or `100755`. Symlinks (`120000`), gitlinks (`160000`) and any other mode stay product.
3. Blob reads (P4). Resolve HEAD once. HEAD is unborn only when `HEAD` is a symbolic ref to a branch that does not exist; any other resolution failure is an error. For a resolved commit, look up the exact path in its tree; a successful lookup with no entry is absent; an entry is read by its object id. Absent or unborn gives `null`. Any resolution, lookup or blob-read error keeps the path product. A staged blob that cannot be read on a non-deletion keeps the path product; an empty blob is content, not a failure. ## Summary

Initial installation commit blocked by prospective scope-cover despite documented pre-activation bootstrap

## Context

Bullhorn MCP consumer repository; Directive engine, pin and content 0.126.1; macOS Codex host. Installation artifacts were created by directive init; no application implementation exists.

## Expected behavior

The documented getting-started step 6 can commit installation artifacts before step 7 promotes and activates the first product scope. Installing Directive should not require a separately merged active setup xBRIEF.

## Actual behavior / gap

The git commit PreToolUse gate rejects the initial installation files with no ready running scope. Creating and activating a scope changes the error to missing positive governing file_scope because the scope is absent from the merge base. isLifecycleOrInstallerRelPath exempts xbrief trees and six managed hook paths but treats AGENTS.md, Taskfile.yml, package.json, package-lock.json and installed skill wrappers as product paths.

## Session notes

Reproduction: directive init in an existing Git repository; stage generated setup files on a feature branch; ask Codex to commit. The docs instruct committing the deposit before activation, while evaluateProspectiveScopeCover requires an active scope and merge-base coverage for these files. Scope-only commit and push worked but did not unblock installation files. Please provide an audited initial-deposit admission or correct the bootstrap workflow without weakening ordinary product-write scope checks.

---
_Filed via `deft feedback:file` from a directive consumer project (Refs #1709 value-feedback gap escalation)._

## Adoption-blocker evidence

- Affected consumer flow / version: Bullhorn MCP; Directive 0.126.1; macOS Codex; `directive init` then commit deposit before first scope activate.
- Alternatives attempted: create/activate a setup scope — error becomes missing merge-base `file_scope` for deposit paths; scope-only commit/push does not unblock AGENTS.md / Taskfile.yml / package.json / skill wrappers.
- Observed recovery cost: initial installation commit blocked; bootstrap docs and PreToolUse gate disagree.
- Triage owner / date: Scott (MScottAdams), 2026-10-22.
